proofs.summary: Every ordered pair of basis vectors must obey the cross reduced-state identity. Testing the individual vectors alone is insufficient.
proofs.bodyHtml: For an orthonormal basis, expanding an arbitrary normalized superposition proves the condition sufficient. Polarization of the diagonal reduced-state identity proves it necessary. Equivalently, for every rank .

proofs.title: Complementary Schmidt-space bound
proofs.summary: Choose a common symmetric t-qubit basis in the maximally entangled Schmidt decomposition of every orthonormal code vector. The cross-reduction condition makes all k(t+1) partner vectors mutually orthogonal in Sym^(N−t)(C²), which has dimension N−t+1.
proofs.bodyHtml: Published in Eq. (52); the complementary Schmidt-space argument applies to every t-AC subspace.

proofs.title: Spin-tensor Gram dimension bound
proofs.summary: Let s=floor(t/2), and choose Hilbert–Schmidt orthonormal spin tensor operators A_α spanning ranks 0,...,s. There are (s+1)² such operators. Every A_α†A_β is a linear combination of tensor ranks ≤2s≤t, so its compression to V is Tr(A_α†A_β) I_V/(N+1)=δ_αβ I_V/(N+1). Therefore the k(s+1)² vectors sqrt(N+1) A_α|ψ_a> are orthonormal in H^(j), of dimension N+1.
proofs.bodyHtml: An independent consequence of the paper’s compression characterization and standard spin-tensor product decomposition; no novelty claim.

The general rectangular-tensor bound excludes dimension three. Hence the analytical plane has optimal dimension.

proofs.title: Molien series give analytical AC subspaces
proofs.summary: Exact single-character spaces of the binary polyhedral groups provide polynomial bases. Their full spans obey the AC conditions, and higher AC orders are checked separately.
proofs.bodyHtml:
Averaging each spin tensor of rank over the rotation group gives zero. The common character phase cancels in every matrix element between two vectors in the same character space, proving the cross conditions for the whole subspace. Different characters are kept separate.

Molien coefficients count independent homogeneous invariant or relative-invariant polynomials. The exported bases are orthonormalized with the exact Dicke inner product, and every ordered reduced cross matrix is checked independently. A constructed dimension does not assert a global maximum.

proofs.title: General analytical prescriptions for second-order AC subspaces
proofs.summary: Three-component radical vectors give dimension floor((N+3)/9) for every N≥6. Prescribed moment weights and quadrilateral phases improve the four-component family to floor((N−1)/8) for every N≥17. These are lower bounds, not general maximality claims.
proofs.bodyHtml:
Choose three separated Dicke indices per vector, with rational probabilities solving normalization, zero first magnetic moment and second moment . A gap of at least three between all occupied indices removes every rank-one and rank-two cross term. The explicit formulas and positivity proof work for every .

The improved four-band prescription uses four coefficients per vector. A rational correction preserves the prescribed first two moments while enabling a quadrilateral of phases to close for each adjacent pair. Exact polynomial coefficient positivity proves for every . Below seventeen this term is dominated by the separated-triple bound, proving the combined inequality throughout . All coefficients are given by arithmetic and square roots, with no numerical root search.

The new formula improves the previous general four-band term by one whenever . Stronger size-specific witnesses remain in use. The existing catalogue intervals are unchanged. A separate moment partition supplies a simpler real radical representative of dimension three at .

proofs.title: Prescribed moment partitions and overlapping compressions
proofs.summary: A convex partition at a fixed moment point produces exact AC2 bases when all used Dicke indices have gaps at least three. Overlapping joint compressions extend this method. Simpler real radical representatives are supplied at N=12 and N=22.

For disjoint support blocks, positive probabilities with these prescribed moments give orthonormal vectors with amplitudes . Global Dicke gaps of at least three annihilate every rank-one and rank-two shift, including the cross terms. The common convex-intersection point must be the specified AC moment point; an arbitrary Tverberg intersection is insufficient.

At twelve qubits a reflection-even and reflection-odd pair on five shared Dicke levels gives a simpler dimension-two basis. At twenty-two qubits two exact two-point distributions and one three-point distribution give a real dimension-three basis. Every ordered two-qubit cross reduction is checked symbolically. The unrestricted maximum is already two at twelve qubits; maximality remains open at twenty-two.

The globally separated-support strategy, even with overlapping basis vectors, obeys . This is a bound on that construction class, not on arbitrary AC2 subspaces. The improved four-band family exceeds its asymptotic density by allowing shifts and cancelling their cross terms with phases.
